name: Plastics pyrolysis (chemical recycling)
applications: feedstock for steam crackers from mixed or contaminated plastic waste
principle: Mixed post-consumer plastic waste, mainly polyolefins, is heated without oxygen so that the polymers crack into a hydrocarbon oil (called TACOIL by Plastic Energy), gas and char. The oil is cleaned and used as feed to steam crackers, where it displaces fossil naphtha and can be counted as recycled content through mass balance.

performance.basis: Plastic Energy and TotalEnergies, expected operational early 2025 (as of January 2022)

source.note: Plastic Energy and TotalEnergies release (Business Wire ID 20220110)

reference_plants.name: Plastic Energy and TotalEnergies advanced recycling plant, Seville
reference_plants.status: no start-up of the new 33,000 t/yr plant was ever announced; Plastic Energy's own current plant list shows only the original Seville plant, operational since 2017; the company entered administration in England in May 2026, emerged in August 2026 with founder Carlos Monreal returning as CEO, and in September 2026 transferred its stake in the TEPEAR joint-venture plant at Grandpuits (15,000 t/yr, operational since March 2026) to TotalEnergies while retaining the Almeria and Seville plants (as of 11 September 2026)

source.note: letsrecycle.com, 11 September 2026 (read 28 October 2026); plant list from plasticenergy.com/operations/ (read 28 October 2026)

advantages: Handles mixed and soiled plastics that mechanical recycling rejects
limitations: Yield losses to char and gas
Recycled content depends on accounting rules
